# Ramp — the numbers

*Generated by `docs/pitches/ramp/numbers.py`. Re-run it to change any input:*

```
api/.venv/Scripts/python ../docs/pitches/ramp/numbers.py --md ../docs/pitches/ramp/numbers.md
api/.venv/Scripts/python ../docs/pitches/ramp/numbers.py --set search_share=0.10 --set lookups_per_day=40
```

Three kinds of number live in this file and they are never mixed:

- **ASSUMED** — an input you may disagree with. Every one has a range and a reason. Section 1.
- **MEASURED** — recorded in this repo or on the live service today. Section 2. Source on every line.
- **HIS** — the founder's friend's own figures: 20% of his time, ~$4 a question. Marked wherever they appear.

## 1. Assumptions — the column you are allowed to argue with

| input | assumed | unit | range | where it comes from / why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hours_per_year` | **2,000** | h/year | 1,800 – 2,200 | Owner-mechanic, full-time. Anchored on Eurostat lfsa_ewhuis 2024: a German full-time self-employed craft/trades worker usually works 44.3 h/week (all self-employed: 45.0). 44.3 x 45 working weeks = 1,994 h. The 45 weeks (5 weeks holiday + public holidays + sick) is the assumed part. |
| `search_share` | **0.20** | of working time | 0.10 – 0.20 | HIS NUMBER, not ours: the founder's friend estimates ~20% of his working time goes to looking for a page. The low end halves it for the sceptic. |
| `working_days` | **230** | days/year | 220 – 240 | 45 working weeks x 5 days, rounded down for odd days off. |
| `lookups_per_day` | **25** | lookups/day | 15 – 40 | How often a mechanic opens a manual. 40/day is the figure the cost report already prices the monthly bill at; 15/day is the sceptic's floor. |
| `rate_de` | **110** | EUR/h | 75 – 125 | German independent-workshop labour rate. motor.com.de 2026: national average EUR 110/h, freie Werkstatt EUR 75-125/h, Vertragswerkstatt EUR 140-195/h. Cross-check from a real German KTM motorcycle workshop: FinkMoto publishes EUR 139/h including 19% VAT = EUR 116.81 net. |
| `rate_us` | **140** | USD/h | 120 – 159 | US independent-shop labour rate. AutoLeap 2026: 'a national benchmark is near $140 for independent shops', range $120-159 across states. |
| `recovery` | **0.70** | of searching time | 0.30 – 0.90 | The fraction of searching time the product actually removes. Not 1.0: the mechanic still has to read the page and decide. 0.30 is the hostile case. |
| `utilisation` | **0.80** | of recovered time | 0.50 – 1 | Recovered hours only become money if there is work waiting to fill them. 1.0 for a booked-out one-man shop, 0.5 for a slow one. |
| `price_de` | **49** | EUR/seat/month | 29 – 99 | What we would charge a workshop per mechanic. Not yet validated by a sale. Payback is so short that the whole range lands in the same week. |
| `price_us` | **59** | USD/seat/month | 39 – 119 | Same, at US rates. |
| `self_employed_hours` | **2,000** | h/year | 1,800 – 2,200 | Hours worked by a self-employed person in the sector. Eurostat publishes hours for EMPLOYEES only; the self-employed are added at this assumed figure. |
| `us_tech_hours` | **1,800** | h/year | 1,700 – 1,900 | US technician working year. No Eurostat equivalent; BLS blocks automated retrieval, so this one is an outright assumption. |
| `usd_per_eur` | **1.08** | USD per EUR | 1.02 – 1.18 | Only used to put our dollar-denominated model cost next to a euro price. Nothing in the argument turns on it. |

## 3. One mechanic, one year

| line | kind | value | formula |
|---|---|---|---|
| working hours in a year | assumed | 2,000 h | `hours_per_year` |
| share spent looking for a page | his number | 20% | `search_share` |
| **hours a year searching** | = product | **400 h** | `hours_per_year x search_share` |
| …as whole working days | derived | 50 days | `400 / 8` |
| …as minutes per working day | derived | 104 min | `search_hours x 60 / working_days` |
| …so one lookup must cost him | derived | **4.2 min** | `search_hours x 60 / (working_days x lookups_per_day)` |
| at the German independent rate | assumed rate | **EUR 44,000/year** | `search_hours x rate_de` |
| at the US independent rate | assumed rate | **$56,000/year** | `search_hours x rate_us` |

**Why the 4.2 minutes matters.** We never assert how long a lookup takes.
We take his 20%, divide by the number of lookups, and *derive* it. 4.2 minutes to find
a torque figure in a 268-page PDF on a phone with dirty hands is not a dramatic claim — it is a boring one.
If you think the 20% is inflated, §7 runs it the other way: pick the minutes and the lookups you believe,
and read off the share of the year they imply.

## 4. From gross exposure to money you would defend

Not every searching hour turns into a billed hour. Two deductions, both assumptions, both arguable:

| step | hours/year | Germany | US | what it means |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gross exposure | 400 h | EUR 44,000 | $56,000 | what a year of searching bills out at |
| x recovery 70% | 280 h | EUR 30,800 | $39,200 | the part the product actually removes |
| x utilisation 80% | 224 h | **EUR 24,640** | **$31,360** | the part that becomes billed work |

Say the small number on stage. **EUR 24,640** is the one we would put in a contract;
EUR 44,000 is the one that is true but flattering.

**Per-shop payback.** Our price is an assumption (EUR 49/seat/month, `price_de`);
the value is the recovered column above.

| mechanics | recovered billable work / year | our price (EUR 49/seat/mo) | price as % of the value | payback | return |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | EUR 24,640 | EUR 588 | 2.39% | **5.5 working days** | 42x |
| **3** | EUR 73,920 | EUR 1,764 | 2.39% | **5.5 working days** | 42x |
| **10** | EUR 246,400 | EUR 5,880 | 2.39% | **5.5 working days** | 42x |

Payback is measured in working days, not months, and it does not improve or worsen with shop size — it is a
per-seat number multiplied by seats. What changes with size is the absolute figure: the ten-mechanic shop is
looking at EUR 246,400 of work it is currently spending on PDFs.

Every row measured against the live service at `https://mechanica.emilvinu.ch/api`.

| step | measured | source |
|---|---|---|
| photo of the bike -> the exact model+year | 5.80 s | live POST /api/identify/photo x3, 2026-09-20: 5.01 / 5.80 / 7.66 s |
| VIN -> the exact model+year | 0.11 s | live POST /api/identify/vin VBKJSA40XXXXXXXXX -> KTM 390 Duke 2024, 2026-09-20 |
| manual metadata (chapters, specs) | 0.09 s | live GET /api/manuals/ktm-390-duke-2023-eu-om, 2026-09-20 |
| plain-words question -> the section and page | 1.59 s | 5 live asks vs mechanica.emilvinu.ch, 2026-09-20 (1.46/1.54/1.59/2.98/4.37) |
| …over 150 controlled queries | mean 1.60 s, p95 3.33 s | api/eval/report.md, 150 queries, sequential, cold cache |
| …the same question a second time | 0.130 s | same run, the same question asked twice: 0.075 s and 0.179 s, $0 |

| **typed or VIN -> the marked page** | **2.03 s** | sum of the rows above |
| **photo -> the marked page** | **7.72 s** | sum of the rows above |

Those end-to-end figures are **machine time on the critical path** — what the service spends, not what a
stopwatch on stage will read. Add the mechanic's own taps and his reading of the page and the stopwatch number
is maybe two to three times that (estimate, not measured). What collapsed is the *finding*, and the finding is
1.59 seconds.

**Before and after, per lookup.** The "before" column is the assumption; everything right of it follows from
the measured 7.7 s. The last two columns are the same saving gross and after the §4 deductions.

| a lookup today (assumed) | with Mechanica (measured) | speed-up | saved at 25 lookups x 230 days | …as a share of the year | gross at the German rate | recovered (§4 deductions applied) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 min | 7.7 s (0.13 min) | 23x | 275 h | 14% | EUR 30,269 | EUR 16,950 |
| 5 min | 7.7 s (0.13 min) | 39x | 467 h | 23% | EUR 51,352 | EUR 28,757 |
| 8 min | 7.7 s (0.13 min) | 62x | 754 h | 38% | EUR 82,977 | EUR 46,467 |
| 12 min | 7.7 s (0.13 min) | 93x | 1,138 h | 57% | EUR 125,144 | EUR 70,080 |

Sanity bound: a row whose share of the year runs past about 25% is describing a mechanic who barely touches a
bike. The 3- and 5-minute rows are the ones to quote.

## 6. The cost side — his bill and ours

| stack at 40 questions/day | $ / question | $ / month | $ / year | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| his lived bill when he tried an LLM | $4.00 | $4,800.00 | $57,600.00 | HIS number: a 500-page manual pasted into a flagship model |
| the same design today, priced out | $8.01 | $9,606.00 | $115,272.00 | 400k tokens past the 272k long-context line, so 2x |
| worst case in the deployed catalog | $12.40 | $14,880.00 | $178,560.00 | live `GET /api/cost` -> `naivePerAsk` |
| ours, every question a written chat answer | $0.0042 | $5.04 | $60.48 | worst case: 248 logged chat answers |
| ours, the default path (question -> the page) | $0.00038 | $0.46 | $5.47 | 150-query eval, cost-log delta |

Ours does not move with page count: the prompt never holds the manual, only the pages BM25 returned.
His did — that is the whole of the $4.00. Plus $0.0951 once per manual
(api/data/mass_report.jsonl, 648 real ingests, paid once per manual), never per question.

**What that does to the unit economics of a seat:**

| what we serve | model cost / seat / year | price / seat / year | gross margin on the AI line | price ÷ cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default path (an ask) | $5.47 | EUR 588 = $635 | **99.14%** | 116x |
| worst case (every question a chat answer) | $60.48 | EUR 588 = $635 | **90.48%** | 11x |

The point for Ramp: the AI line item is
**9.5% of the subscription in the
worst case** and 0.86% on the
default path. It is not a cost that scales badly with usage — it is a rounding error that scales with the number
of distinct manuals, and there are only so many motorcycles. Every AI budget line in this company is a fixed
cost in disguise; the variable one is the ingest, $0.0951 a manual, paid once and shared by
every shop that ever opens that bike.

**(b) If only half the searching time is recoverable.** Rows are how much of the searching time the product

| recovery \ utilisation | 50% | 80% | 100% |

Every cell in that table pays back a seat inside one working month. The pitch does not depend on the

**(c) If his 20% is really 5%.**

| share of the year spent searching | hours/year | gross at the shop rate | recovered (after recovery x utilisation) | payback on a seat |
|---|---|---|---|---|

At **5%** — a quarter of what he says — a seat still pays for itself in under
22 working days.

## 8. The bigger picture

Hours are built from Eurostat's own *hours worked by employees* where it publishes them, plus self-employed
people at an assumed 2,000 h/year (`self_employed_hours`). Two money columns on purpose: **value added per hour** is Eurostat's own figure and is
the defensible one; **the shop labour rate** is what the customer is charged and is the flattering one.

| region | shops (repair of cars + motorcycles) | people working in them | hours worked / year | lost to searching at 20% | **at sector value added / hour** | at the shop labour rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Germany** | 54,470 | 308,914 | 447 M h | **89 M h** | **EUR 4.4 bn** | EUR 9.8 bn |
| **EU-27** | 540,394 | 1,527,411 | 2.61 bn h | **522 M h** | **EUR 14.7 bn** | EUR 57.4 bn † |
| **US** | 315,404 | 600,406 | 1.08 bn h | **216 M h** | not published | $30.3 bn |

† The EU shop-rate column applies the *German* rate across 27 countries and is therefore too high — Eastern European labour rates are a fraction of it. Use the value-added column, which is each sector's own Eurostat figure (DE cars EUR 48.82/h, DE motorcycles EUR 50.95/h, EU cars EUR 27.34/h, EU motorcycles EUR 39.68/h).

Cross-check on the German shop count: listflix.de counted 40,968 Autowerkstätten on
2026-09-20 against Eurostat's 49,922 enterprises in NACE G45.2 for 2024 — different
definitions, same order of magnitude.

**And the part of it that is a business for us** — seats, not saved hours:

| region | seats (persons employed in the sector) | price / seat / month | seat revenue if every seat bought |
|---|---|---|---|
| Germany | 308,914 | EUR 49 | **EUR 182 M/year** |
| EU-27 | 1,527,411 | EUR 49 | **EUR 898 M/year** |
| US | 600,406 | $59 | **$425 M/year** |

We do not claim every seat. The reachable wedge is the independent shop: Eurostat puts
6 people in the average German car-repair enterprise and
5 in the average motorcycle one, and listflix puts 49.4% of
German car workshops at a single sole proprietor. This is a market of one- to six-person shops — which is
exactly the shop in the story, and exactly the shop nobody sells software to.

## 9. Why the time saving is allowed to count

A time saving nobody trusts is not a saving — he goes and checks the manual anyway, and you have added a step.

| gate | measured | source |
|---|---|---|
| right section first, in-scope queries | **100%** of 130 | `api/eval/report.md` |
| off-topic questions returned empty instead of guessed at | **100%** of 20 | `api/eval/report.md` |
| chat quotes verbatim on the page they name | **100%** of 43 | `api/eval/chat-report.md` |

The answer is the manufacturer's page with a marker on the line. If we are wrong, he sees it in half a second,
because he is looking at the manual and not at a paragraph.

### Known weaknesses, stated rather than hidden

- **`lookups_per_day` has no source.** It is the load-bearing assumption in §7(a). We derive the minutes per
  lookup from his 20% rather than asserting both, but one of the two has to be assumed.
- **`recovery` and `utilisation` have no source either.** They exist to stop us quoting EUR 44,000 as
  if it were revenue.
- **The US technician count is second-hand.** BLS blocks automated retrieval, so 600,406 comes
  from AutoLeap quoting BLS, not from BLS directly.
- **`poidata.io` is the weakest source in the file.** The US motorcycle dealer count should be treated as an
  order of magnitude, and it barely moves the market number next to 307,058 car shops.
- **p50 for an ask is not in the committed eval report** — it publishes mean 1.60 s and
  p95 3.33 s. The 1.59 s median is our own 5-query live run today.
  `api/eval/run.py --json` records per-query `seconds` if you want the real p50 over 150.
- **The price is not validated by a sale.** EUR 49/seat/month is what we would charge, not
  what anyone has paid.
